custom-calc.description: A scratch-built calculator: a 30-pin ESP32 development board, 20 Cherry MX-style keys and a 4-inch ST7796S TFT on a custom 153.5 × 83.5 mm KiCad board, inside a case modeled in SolidWorks. The 20 keys share nine GPIO pins as a 5 × 4 matrix. The firmware pulls one row low at a time, reads the four pulled-up columns with a 10 ms debounce, and drives the display over SPI with the TFT_eSPI library. A September 2026 board revision moved two pins: GPIO35 is input-only, and GPIO12 is a strapping pin sampled at boot.
highlights: ESP32 dev board, 20 keys in a 5 × 4 matrix on 9 GPIO
4" ST7796S TFT, 480 × 320, SPI at 80 MHz
153.5 × 83.5 mm two-layer KiCad board
SolidWorks case: body, key plate, base, bezel, alcove and keycaps
Arduino firmware on TFT_eSPI with a key-matrix tester
custom-calc.note: Renders made in Blender from the project's own Calculator.blend; the screen shows the firmware's test graphics.

projects.title: HOLLOWDEEP
projects.summary: A gothic first-person dungeon crawler with its own software 3D renderer written in Lua, an endless procedural dungeon, a grid inventory and a skill tree.
projects.description: HOLLOWDEEP is a gothic, medieval first-person dungeon crawler for the SUGAR engine. Everything on screen comes from a software polygon renderer written in Lua: a free-look camera, a per-pixel depth buffer, perspective-correct textures and smooth vertex lighting, with portal visibility so only the cells you can see are drawn. The dungeon is infinite, built from 16 × 16-cell chunks generated from a world seed and stitched together through matching exits, with stairs, pits, ledges and balconies. On top of Quake-style movement sit a Diablo II-style HUD, a Tarkov-style grid inventory, loot chests, a merchant in every 4 × 4 block of chunks, and three skill trees of warfare, marksmanship and sorcery.
highlights: Software 3D rasterizer in Lua: depth buffer, textures, vertex lighting
Infinite chunked dungeon across five themes
Eight enemy types with line-of-sight and flow-field pathfinding
45 item bases, 35 affixes, a rotate-to-fit grid inventory
Three skill trees: Warfare, Marksman, Sorcery
49 synthesized sound effects; ~6 ms per busy frame with LuaJIT

projects.title: DEEPWELL
projects.summary: A 3D block puzzle down a well, in two editions: a PICO-8 cartridge and DEEPWELL DX for SUGAR, with lit cubes, particles and VIGIL, a wax-and-fire mode.
projects.description: DEEPWELL is a 3D block puzzle: pieces built from cubes fall into a 5 × 5 well, 12 layers deep, seen from straight above in perspective. You turn, tip and roll them in three dimensions and fill a whole layer to clear it. The PICO-8 edition is a single 128 × 128 cartridge with wireframe and flat-shaded 3D, two modes, high scores and a Virtual Boy-style red look, running at 60 fps in about 5,100 of PICO-8's 8,192 tokens. DEEPWELL DX for SUGAR redraws it at 480 × 270 with solid lit cubes, parallax, a glass falling piece, particles and a synthesized soundtrack. It also adds VIGIL, where the pieces are candle wax, every fifth piece is a flame, and fire spreads through touching wax of the same color.
highlights: 5 × 5 well, 12 layers deep; turn, tip and roll in 3D
PICO-8 cart: ~5,100 of 8,192 tokens at 60 fps
Painter's-order 3D with no sorting: deepest layer first
DX edition: 480 × 270, 103-colour lit palette, parallax
VIGIL mode: wax chains that burn by colour
16 synthesized sound effects and two music loops

projects.title: Custom MP3 Player
projects.summary: A pocket-sized, cylindrical MP3 player built around an ESP32-S3, with a long color bar display and three gear-driven ring knobs. In the design phase.
projects.description: A hobby build inspired by Sony's NW-E507 'stick' Walkman: a single tube about 40 mm across and 130–160 mm long, with a 2.25-inch, 76 × 284 color IPS bar display behind a semi-translucent shell and three ring knobs the full width of the tube. A gear inside each ring drives a small rotary encoder in the body, and a long spine PCB runs down the center beside the 18650 cell. The parts list is final and a SolidWorks mock assembly of the housing and internals is in progress; the PCBs and firmware come next.
highlights: Adafruit ESP32-S3 Feather with 2 MB PSRAM for MP3 decoding
2.25" 76 × 284 IPS bar TFT over SPI
Three no-detent Bourns PEC11R encoders at ~2.5:1 through the rings
TLV320DAC3100 I²S DAC and headphone amp
2200 mAh 18650 cell with a MAX17048 fuel gauge
Spine board and display board joined by two 10-pin ribbons
projects.note: Concept renders generated in Blender from the README's dimensions and parts list, not from the SolidWorks model.

projects.title: Market Dashboard
projects.summary: A live local dashboard of tech stocks and world markets: a dot-matrix world map, a globe, a heatmap and charts in a red HUD look, fed by Yahoo Finance.
projects.description: A standalone dashboard that tracks tech stocks and world market indexes. A small Python server pulls prices through the yfinance library and serves a single page: index tiles, a scrolling ticker, a dot-matrix world map and globe, a rotating price-history chart with headlines, a market heatmap and each stock's place in its 52-week range. Index levels refresh every minute, currency rates every five and price history every fifteen. If Yahoo can't be reached, the page falls back to a saved snapshot so it always draws.
highlights: Python server with a vanilla JavaScript front end
Refresh: prices 60 s, FX 5 min, history 15 min, headlines 10 min
Offline snapshot fallback
Tickers, indexes and chart series set in one config.json
projects.note: Screenshots taken from the offline snapshot mode.

projects.title: Custom Keyboard PCB
projects.summary: A custom mechanical keyboard PCB around a Teensy 4.0: a 16 × 6 key matrix read through an MCP23017 I/O expander, a small color display and a rotary encoder.
projects.description: A custom mechanical keyboard board built around a Teensy 4.0, with a 16-column by 6-row key matrix (up to 96 keys, one diode per switch), a 1.14-inch ST7789 color display below the keys and a rotary encoder with a push button. The design needs about 30 GPIO but the Teensy's through-hole edge pins only offer 24, so the 16 column lines go to an MCP23017 I²C expander. A full six-row scan still finishes well under a millisecond at 400 kHz. The schematic is drawn; PCB layout and firmware come next.
highlights: Teensy 4.0 with native USB
16 × 6 matrix, one diode per switch
MCP23017 reads all 16 columns in one I²C transaction
1.14" ST7789 135 × 240 display and an EC11 encoder
